codebase.title: legume — guided-mode expansion for photonic crystal slabs
codebase.fingerprint_algorithm: SHA-256 over typed sorted regular-file paths+bytes and symlink paths+safe targets

agent_authored.description: legume (le GUided Mode Expansion) computes the photonic band structure, radiative linewidths and quality factors of photonic crystal slabs — dielectric slabs patterned with a periodic array of holes or pillars, possibly stacked in several layers. It does so by the guided-mode expansion: the electromagnetic field is expanded in the guided modes of the equivalent unpatterned slab, the patterning enters as a Fourier-transformed inverse permittivity, and the resulting Hermitian matrix is diagonalised per Bloch wavevector. Expanding in guided modes rather than discretising space gives legume direct access to the quasi-guided resonances above the light line, which leak into the radiation continuum and are awkward to isolate in a first-principles time-domain or frequency-domain solver, and it obtains their quality factors from perturbation theory in the same pass. A plane-wave expansion for purely two-dimensional crystals and an exciton–polariton layer built on the photonic bands ship in the same package. Its distinguishing feature is that the whole calculation is differentiable: switching the numeric backend to autograd makes every output a function of every geometric input, so the gradient of a cavity's quality factor with respect to the positions of all of its holes comes from one reverse-mode pass, which is what makes the package a tool for inverse design rather than only for analysis.
evidence: README.md (upstream): 'legume (le GUided Mode Expansion) is a python implementation of the GME method for photonic crystal slabs, including multi-layer structures.'
Minkov et al., 'Inverse design of photonic crystals through automatic differentiation', ACS Photonics 7(7) 1729 (2020).
Zanotti et al., 'Legume: A free implementation of the guided-mode expansion method for photonic crystal slabs', Comput. Phys. Commun. 304 (2024) 109286.

pitfalls.symptom: Every example notebook fails at its first legume call with AttributeError: module 'legume' has no attribute 'Lattice', and bare `pytest` at the repository root dies with 9 collection errors ('import file mismatch' on duplicate test basenames).
pitfalls.workaround: Both symptoms have one cause: docs/examples/legume/ is a committed stale copy of an older repository root with no __init__.py, so it is picked up as a namespace package that shadows the installed legume whenever the working directory is docs/examples/, and its 9 test_*.py files collide by basename with the real tests/ when pytest scans from the root. Run the suite as `python -m pytest tests` (never bare `pytest`) and execute notebooks from a directory other than docs/examples/ (copying the .ipynb elsewhere is enough; the notebooks reference no relative paths).

pitfalls.symptom: Two runs of the same input on the same build give different bits when the BLAS thread count differs; the graded values are stable for a fixed thread count.
pitfalls.workaround: Pin OPENBLAS_NUM_THREADS, OMP_NUM_THREADS, MKL_NUM_THREADS, NUMEXPR_NUM_THREADS and VECLIB_MAXIMUM_THREADS to a fixed value in the check, never read from the host. Measured at gmax=7: 1 thread versus 8 threads leaves every frequency above 1e-6 agreeing to 9.6e-14 relative, but the bits differ. Matches the existing pitfall blas-threads-follow-the-host-core-count.

pitfalls.symptom: Relative error on gme.freqs explodes to 34-51% while the absolute difference is only 4e-08.
pitfalls.workaround: At the Gamma point the two lowest bands are numerically zero (1.94e-08 and 7.40e-08 at gmax=7), so relative error on them is meaningless noise. Restricted to |freq| > 1e-6, the same comparison is 9.6e-14. Upstream already works around this in its own tests by slicing off band 0 (gme.freqs[0, 1:]) and adding a 1e-10 floor to the denominator. Any pointwise policy needs an absolute floor or must exclude the near-zero modes.

pitfalls.symptom: Perturbing an input by two ulps moves the output by ~1e-14 relative, and perturbing by 2000 ulps moves it by only ~1.2e-13: the response does not scale with the perturbation.
pitfalls.workaround: legume/gme/slab_modes.py finds guided modes with scipy brentq under gmode_tol (default 1e-12), so the output carries a root-finder tolerance floor of about 1e-14 relative rather than propagating the input smoothly. Measured ratios of output move to input perturbation: 28.8x at 2 ulps, 2.4x at 20, 0.36x at 200, 0.27x at 2000. The floor is mild and well below any sensible bound, but a two-ulp variant spread is not a meaningful calibration here; set bounds from the physics, not from the variant.
Install memory_profiler. It is used by one example notebook but appears in no dependency list of the project, neither in pyproject.toml dependencies nor in the test, autodiff or docs extras.

pitfalls.symptom: Tests fail with FileNotFoundError on tests/data/*.mat when run from any directory other than the repository root.
pitfalls.workaround: Every reference-loading test hardcodes a relative path of the form 'dot-slash tests/data/...'. The suite must be invoked with the repository root as the working directory.

pitfalls.symptom: Three of the fourteen example notebooks fail on numpy 2 while the pytest suite is unaffected.
pitfalls.workaround: Upstream removed its numpy<2 constraint at 1.0.3 (commit 14b7b7e) and its CI runs only `python -m pytest tests`, so the examples were never exercised against numpy 2. modules.title: legume — guided-mode expansion for photonic crystal slabs
entrypoints: legume.GuidedModeExp(phc, gmax=...).run(kpoints=..., gmode_inds=..., numeig=..., compute_im=...) — the guided-mode expansion: photonic bands, radiative linewidths and quality factors of a multi-layer photonic crystal slab
legume.PlaneWaveExp(layer, gmax=...).run(kpoints=...) — plane-wave expansion for a purely 2D photonic crystal
legume.PhotCryst, Lattice, Layer, Circle, Poly, Ring — the geometry front end that every run is built from
legume.set_backend('autograd') — switches the numeric backend so every output is differentiable with respect to every geometric input
legume.ExcitonSchroedEq and legume.HopfieldPol — exciton and exciton-polariton coupling on top of a photonic band structure
modules.expensive_path: One GuidedModeExp.run splits, measured by cProfile on a hexagonal slab over a 31-point G-M-K-G path, between two costs that scale differently. GuidedModeExp._construct_mat (legume/gme/gme.py:523) builds the Hermitian expansion matrix from the Fourier-transformed inverse permittivity and the slab's guided modes; inside it GuidedModeExp._compute_guided (gme.py:356) solves the transcendental slab dispersion relation with scipy brentq through legume/gme/slab_modes.py, 3,209 root-finds and 19,329 scalar evaluations of D22 at gmax=7. numpy.linalg.eigh then diagonalises that matrix. Construction dominates at small basis size and the eigensolve dominates at large: eigh is 22% of the run at gmax=5 (n_G=61), 48% at gmax=7 (n_G=127), 66% at gmax=9 (n_G=211), 74% at gmax=11 (n_G=313) and 82% at gmax=13 (n_G=451), crossing over at about gmax=7. The eigensolve is a LAPACK call in numpy, outside the vendored tree; the code this module owns is the matrix construction, the Fourier factorization of the permittivity in legume/phc/ and legume/gme/matrix_elements.py, the brentq guided-mode solver in legume/gme/slab_modes.py, and the custom autograd primitives for eigh and eigsh in legume/primitives.py.
modules.rationale: The whole-codebase default. legume is one pip-installable Python package of 8,587 production lines in 25 files, with one build (pip install -e), one test suite (python -m pytest tests) and one community of users. Its subpackages are stages of a single calculation rather than separate packages: legume/phc/ builds the geometry and its Fourier transform, legume/gme/ and legume/pwe/ expand the fields in that geometry, legume/pol/ and legume/exc/ couple excitons to the bands the expansion produced, and legume/primitives.py and legume/backend.py switch all of them between numpy and autograd. None of them has its own entry point, its own input/output contract or its own test target: the ten test files all drive the package through the same top-level legume namespace, and legume/pwe/ has no test of its own at all. A multi-module cut would fail both conditions the skill sets, so the cut is one module over paths ['.'].
excluded: legume/viz.py (1,495 lines) and legume/print_utils.py, legume/print_backend.py, legume/gds.py (452 lines together): plotting, pretty-printing and GDS export. Owned by the module but no check grades them; they produce figures and console text, not physics.

docs/examples/legume/ (22 files, 3.7 MB, 618 lines of stale Python): a committed stale copy of an older repository root. Vendored byte-for-byte with the rest of the tree but excluded from the test survey; it is not an official test family.
hazards: UPSTREAM DEFECT, autograd through radiative coupling. legume/gme/gme.py:1720 and :1743 add an autograd ArrayBox in place into a plain numpy array allocated by bd.zeros, so any differentiated run with compute_im=True (the default) raises TypeError. This breaks tests/test_gme_grad.py and example notebooks 06 and 08 — the tutorials for the package's headline feature, gradients of the quality factor. Reproduced identically on numpy 1.26.4 and 2.5.3, so it is not a numpy 2 regression; present since commit d663dd5 (2020-03-12) and in every tag. A two-line out-of-place rewrite makes the shipped test pass. Differentiation with compute_im=False works and gives correct gradients.

UPSTREAM DEFECT, a shadowing stale directory. docs/examples/legume/ has no __init__.py and shadows the installed package whenever the working directory is docs/examples/, so all 14 example notebooks fail at their first legume call when run where the documentation says to run them; its 9 test_*.py files also collide by basename with tests/, so bare `pytest` at the repository root dies with 9 collection errors. Only `python -m pytest tests` works.

Three of fourteen example notebooks (05, 15, 16) fail on numpy 2 for reasons inside the notebooks rather than the library: size-1-array %-formatting in 05 and 16, an int64 overflow (2*10**19) in 15. All three run on numpy 1.26.4. Upstream dropped its numpy<2 cap at 1.0.3 and its CI runs only `python -m pytest tests`, so the examples were never exercised against numpy 2.

Near-zero observables at high symmetry. At the Gamma point the two lowest bands are numerically zero (1.94e-08 and 7.40e-08 at gmax=7) and their relative error between two legitimate thread settings is 34-51% while the absolute difference is 4e-08. Every frequency above 1e-6 agrees to 9.6e-14 in the same comparison. Upstream's own tests slice off band 0 and add a 1e-10 floor. Any pointwise policy needs an absolute floor or must exclude those modes.

BLAS thread count changes the graded bits. Runs are byte-identical across processes at a fixed thread count and differ at the bit level between 1 and 8 threads. The thread count must be pinned by the check and never read from the host.

Root-finder tolerance floor. Guided modes come from scipy brentq under gmode_tol (default 1e-12), so the output carries a floor of about 1e-14 relative and does not respond proportionally to a small input perturbation: a two-ulp change moves the output 28.8x its own size, a 2000-ulp change only 0.27x. A two-ulp variant spread is therefore not meaningful calibration evidence here.

Eigenvector gauge. numpy.linalg.eigh fixes no phase convention. Between 1 and 8 BLAS threads the eigenvectors stayed in the same gauge (overlap magnitude 1.0, phase below 1e-22 rad), which shows determinism within one LAPACK build rather than agreement across implementations; a different eigensolver may legitimately return a different phase, so eigenvectors must not be graded raw.

A credential-shaped string is vendored. docs/examples/legume/README.md carries a Travis CI badge URL ending ?token=ZCPktA3Ki2eYVXYnfbrz. It is upstream's own published file for a service the project no longer uses, it is already public, and byte-for-byte vendoring keeps it; naming it here so a reviewer reads the assessment rather than discovering the string.

primary_inputs: A PhotCryst geometry: a Lattice (square, rectangular, hexagonal or an explicit pair of primitive vectors), one or more Layers each with a thickness d and background permittivity eps_b, and Shapes (Circle, Poly, Square, Ring) carved into them, plus the permittivities of the lower and upper claddings.
A truncation of the plane-wave basis: gmax, the reciprocal-lattice cutoff, with truncate_g selecting the 'tbt' (two-by-two) or 'abs' (absolute) retention rule; this sets n_G and with it the cost.
A list of Bloch wavevectors, usually a path through the Brillouin zone from Lattice.bz_path.

Run options: gmode_inds (which guided bands of the effective slab to include), numeig (how many eigenvalues to keep), compute_im (whether to evaluate radiative losses), kz_symmetry and symm_thr (vertical-plane symmetry separation), use_sparse (dense or sparse eigensolver), and the guided-mode solver settings gmode_step, gmode_tol and gmode_npts.
primary_outputs: gme.freqs — real eigenfrequencies in units of c/a, one array per k-point: the photonic band structure.
gme.freqs_im — imaginary parts of the eigenfrequencies, from which the quality factor Q = freq/(2*freqs_im) follows; produced only when compute_im is true.
gme.eigvecs — the expansion coefficients of each mode over the guided-mode/plane-wave basis, from which real-space fields are reconstructed.
gme.rad_coup — coupling constants of each quasi-guided mode to the TE and TM radiative channels in the lower and upper claddings.
For the exciton–polariton path, HopfieldPol eigenvalues and Hopfield coefficients: the mixed photon–exciton energies.
With the autograd backend, the gradient of any of the above with respect to any geometric input.
algorithm_stages: Geometry and Fourier factorization: legume/phc/ assembles lattice, layers and shapes and computes the Fourier transform of the permittivity (each shape contributes an analytic form factor), then inverts the resulting matrix to obtain eps_inv_mat.

Guided modes of the effective slab: legume/gme/slab_modes.py solves the transcendental dispersion relation of the unpatterned three-layer slab for each in-plane wavevector magnitude with scipy brentq under gmode_tol, giving the basis the expansion uses.

Matrix construction: legume/gme/gme.py:523 _construct_mat, with the matrix elements in legume/gme/matrix_elements.py, assembles the Hermitian expansion matrix from eps_inv_mat and the guided-mode profiles.
Diagonalisation: numpy.linalg.eigh (or a sparse variant when use_sparse is set) returns eigenfrequencies and expansion coefficients.
Radiative losses: legume/gme/gme.py:1588 _compute_rad_components evaluates the coupling of each quasi-guided mode to the radiative continuum, giving freqs_im and the quality factors.
Optional exciton coupling: legume/exc/ solves the exciton Schroedinger equation on the same lattice and legume/pol/ diagonalises the Hopfield matrix that mixes excitons with the photonic modes.
Differentiation: legume/backend.py swaps numpy for autograd.numpy throughout, and legume/primitives.py supplies the custom vector-Jacobian products for eigh and eigsh that autograd does not provide.
unique_responsibilities: The guided-mode expansion itself: building and diagonalising the expansion matrix and extracting quasi-guided resonances above the light line together with their radiative linewidths.
Analytic Fourier transforms of the patterned permittivity for circles, polygons, squares and rings on an arbitrary 2D lattice.
The brentq solve for the guided modes of a multi-layer slab, including the bracketing strategy that finds every root of the dispersion relation.
Symmetry separation of photonic modes with respect to horizontal (xy) and vertical (kz) mirror planes, which is what makes even and odd bands separable and is the subject of the 2024 CPC paper.
Custom reverse-mode derivatives of the Hermitian eigenproblem (legume/primitives.py), which is what makes end-to-end gradients of band structures and quality factors possible.
Exciton and exciton–polariton coupling on top of the computed photonic bands.
not_responsible_for: legume/viz.py (1,495 lines) and legume/print_utils.py, legume/print_backend.py, legume/gds.py (452 lines together): plotting, pretty-printing and GDS export. Owned by the module but no check grades them; they produce figures and console text, not physics.

docs/examples/legume/ (22 files, 3.7 MB, 618 lines of stale Python): a committed stale copy of an older repository root. Vendored byte-for-byte with the rest of the tree but excluded from the test survey; it is not an official test family.
The dense Hermitian eigendecomposition itself: numpy.linalg.eigh is a LAPACK call in a dependency, not code this tree owns. It is 22% of a run at gmax=5 and 82% at gmax=13.
Meshing or spatial discretisation of any kind: the method is a modal expansion, so there is no grid.
Time-domain propagation, nonlinear optics and dispersive or lossy materials: permittivities are real and frequency-independent.
modules.differences: Single module: there is nothing to differentiate it from. The cut is the whole codebase over paths ['.'] under the skill's whole-codebase default. legume is one pip-installable package with one build, one test suite and one namespace; its subpackages are consecutive stages of a single calculation rather than packages in their own right, none has an independent entry point or input/output contract, and legume/pwe/ has no test of its own at all, so a multi-module cut would fail both conditions the skill requires.
evidence: cProfile of GuidedModeExp.run on a hexagonal slab over a 31-point G-M-K-G path: _construct_mat versus numpy.linalg.eigh is 0.28 s against 0.08 s at gmax=5 (n_G=61), 0.65 against 0.59 at gmax=7 (127), 1.35 against 2.63 at gmax=9 (211), 2.61 against 7.43 at gmax=11 (313), 4.54 against 21.63 at gmax=13 (451).
The ten files of tests/ all import from the top-level legume namespace; none imports a subpackage directly except legume.utils.
legume/pwe/ (370 lines) has no test in tests/; only example notebooks 02 and 05 exercise it.
pyproject.toml declares one distribution, legume-gme, with packages legume, legume.exc, legume.gme, legume.phc, legume.pol, legume.pwe.

covers: Guided-mode expansion against independent implementations: six .mat references from the authors' MATLAB GME code and gme_gx_both.out, 10,184 lines from the Fortran GME code of Univ. di Pavia.
Symmetry separation with respect to a vertical kz plane, dense and sparse solver paths, 4,000 mode frequencies compared (test_even_odd_separation).
Guided modes of a multi-layer grating against guided_modes_grating.npy (test_guided_modes).
Exciton–polariton energies against three Polariton_*.npy references (test_polariton).
Analytic Fourier transform of a polygon (test_shapes) and the autograd vjps of eigh and eigsh against finite differences (test_primitives).
The 14 example notebooks cover plane-wave expansion, multi-layer gratings, band diagrams, BICs and Q factors, polarization mixing, excitons and polaritons, and autograd optimization.
known_gaps: legume/pwe/ (370 lines, the 2D plane-wave expansion) has no test in tests/ at all; it is exercised only by example notebooks 02 and 05, and 05 fails on numpy 2.
legume/viz.py (1,495 lines), print_utils.py, print_backend.py and gds.py (452 lines together) have no test; they produce figures, console text and GDS output.

tests/test_gme_grad.py fails at this pin on an upstream defect (TypeError at legume/gme/gme.py:1720), so the only end-to-end gradient test of GuidedModeExp does not pass. The two autograd tests that do pass, in test_primitives.py, exercise the eigh/eigsh primitives directly rather than through an expansion.
No notebook ships expected output, so any check derived from one authors its reference from the pinned build.

How the counts above are defined, since two frameworks are mixed. test_files 24 = 10 pytest files plus 14 example notebooks; test_definitions and collected_items 27 = 13 pytest test functions plus 14 notebooks, one per notebook because a notebook has no finer official unit. inner_cases 8 counts graded stages inside a single test function that a check could reasonably separate: the dense and sparse solver paths in test_even_odd_separation (2), and the two k-points asserted separately in each of test_gme_te, test_gme_tm and test_gme_te-tm (6). The three functions of test_gme_1layer are already counted as definitions, not as inner cases. No deeper subdivision was measured.
execution: python -m pytest tests on python 3.14.6, numpy 2.5.3, scipy 1.18.1, BLAS threads pinned to 1: 12 passed, 1 failed, 54.2 s. Longest test 35.3 s (test_even_odd_separation), then 12.0 s (test_polariton) and 3.2 s (test_guided_modes); the remaining ten are under 0.7 s each.

The same suite on the control environment python 3.11.10, numpy 1.26.4, scipy 1.13.1: 12 passed, 1 failed, 89.2 s — the same single failure, which is how the defect was shown not to be a numpy 2 regression.

Reference agreement measured rather than assumed: max relative difference 2.844e-07, 3.091e-07 and 3.119e-07 against gme_square_te.mat, gme_square_tm.mat and gme_square_te-tm.mat over bands 1..9, i.e. about 6.5 significant digits, against upstream's own bound of 1e-4.

9 of 14 example notebooks execute clean in 3.0 to 71.6 s each. Of the five that do not: 06 and 08 hit the gme.py:1720 defect, 05, 15 and 16 hit numpy 2 incompatibilities in their own code, and 07 needs memory_profiler, which is in no dependency list.

Determinism: byte-identical over two runs in one process and over two separate processes at a fixed BLAS thread count; different bits between 1 and 8 threads, with every frequency above 1e-6 still agreeing to 9.6e-14 relative.

known_review_gaps: DEVIATION FROM THE PIN — READ codebase-reports/legume/DEVIATIONS.md FIRST. code/legume/ is NOT byte-for-byte upstream and is the first vendored tree in this benchmark that is not. The complete deviation is 93 files where the pin has 115: four in-place accumulations rewritten out-of-place (legume/gme/gme.py:1720 and :1743, legume/utils.py:28, legume/phc/layer.py:175 — six lines changed, four removed), and the deletion of docs/examples/legume/, a 22-file 3.7 MB fossil copy of an older repository root that contains no Python module. No file was added. Each change is isolated in its own commit, and `git diff 8494b98 HEAD -- code/legume/` is the deviation and nothing else. The four line edits fix a defect present since 2020 that made every differentiated run with compute_im=True raise TypeError; they cannot move a graded value on the numpy backend, measured: freqs, freqs_im and a reconstructed real-space field are sha256-identical to the pristine tree. The deletion fixes two further defects: it removes a namespace package that shadowed the installed legume for any notebook run from docs/examples/ (all 14 failed there) and nine test basenames that collided with tests/ (bare pytest gave nine collection errors; now 13 collected, 0 errors). Directed by the codebase owner; upstream was deliberately not contacted.

Two of the four upstream defects found at this pin are fixed by the deletion above rather than described as live: docs/examples/legume/ shadowed the installed package for notebooks run from their documented location, and its nine stale test basenames broke bare pytest at the repository root. Its README also carried the payload's only credential-shaped string, a defunct read-only Travis badge token that upstream had already removed from the real README in their PR #73. All three go away with the directory.

Four upstream defects were reproduced at this pin, none reported upstream (by the owner's instruction, this tree carries the fix for the first instead): the autograd/compute_im TypeError at gme.py:1720 and :1743, the shadowing stale directory and the pytest basename collision it causes, three notebooks broken on numpy 2 after the numpy<2 cap was dropped at 1.0.3, and one notebook needing an undeclared memory_profiler dependency.
open_questions: Check sizing and what it measures. numpy.linalg.eigh is 22% of a run at gmax=5 and 82% at gmax=13, and it is a LAPACK call in a dependency rather than code this tree owns. Sizing therefore decides what fraction of a check's graded runtime is legume's own Python. A realistic 31-k-point band diagram with radiative losses takes 18 s at gmax=9 and 50 s at gmax=11, both far inside the 300 s per-check line, so the choice is not forced by runtime. This is for the human at STOP 4, not settled here.
Whether the three notebooks that fail only on numpy 2 should be made suitable by pinning numpy<2 in the image, or recorded as unsuitable with their reason.

Whether a check should grade the gradient-of-Q path. It now works: with the three-line fix the whole suite passes and the gradient of the summed Q factors agrees with finite differences to 2.7e-02. The remaining question is whether a check should depend on a path that only works because this tree deviates from its pin, or should stay on the two primitive-level vjp tests that pass on the pristine tree.
